definition: A dataset consisting of paired instructions (or prompts) and corresponding desired responses, used for instruction tuning a language model.
details: Instruction datasets can be human-written, model-generated (synthetic), or a combination of both, and their quality and diversity significantly influence how well a fine-tuned model follows real-world user instructions.

explainer.lead: An instruction dataset pairs instructions or prompts with the desired responses and is used to instruction-tune a language model. Its quality and diversity strongly shape how well the tuned model follows real-world user instructions.

tiers.eli5: It is a big set of practice questions paired with the answers you wish the model would give, used to teach it to follow requests.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers fine-tune on these pairs to improve instruction following, choosing between human-written, model-generated, and mixed data. A pitfall is that poor quality or low diversity in the dataset limits how well the model handles real user instructions.
tiers.paperLevel: An instruction dataset consists of paired instructions (or prompts) and corresponding desired responses. It can be human-written, model-generated (synthetic), or a combination, and its quality and diversity significantly influence instruction-following performance after fine-tuning.

explainer.example: A pair such as the instruction 'Summarise this email' plus a concise summary written as the desired response is one entry in an instruction dataset.
